set.descent_text: Two ways off exist from the top of pitch 10, near the Der Major ledge. One is to traverse the ledge right and climb out through a loose 5.10+ chimney to the summit plateau, then walk off. The other is to rappel the route with two ropes; the line drops straight down below the pitch 5 anchor, where retreat back up would be very hard, and the last rappel lands on the ramp at the start, followed by fourth-class downclimbing to the ground. Both are serious in bad weather or darkness, and the rappels are awkward and often angle.
set.approach: This is a long backcountry trip of roughly 14 to 16 miles each way from the Big Sandy trailhead, with Hailey Pass crossed in the later part of the walk. The trail ends among the boulders and meadows below the wall, and parties usually camp right at its foot. The other way in is from the Dickinson Park side. The route takes the left-hand part of the northeast face, beginning with a right-leaning ramp and then the wishbone-shaped crack system.

review.notes: Descent options and rappel character from the route page; Der Major leading right to the summit plateau from the first-ascent account. Walk-off path beyond the plateau is not described, so none is given.

set.descent_text: The route ends at an anchor at the top of pitch 2. Rappel from there to the large ledge system between the start of pitch 1 and the start of pitch 2, using a long single rope, then scramble back around to the foot of the route.
set.approach: This is a long backcountry trip of roughly 14 to 16 miles each way from the Big Sandy trailhead, with Hailey Pass crossed in the later part of the walk. The trail ends among the boulders and meadows below the wall, and parties usually camp right at its foot. The other way in is from the Dickinson Park side. The route is a two-pitch crack on the far left (east) side of the wall, close to Cache Pirates and starting from the ground, with a splitter first pitch.

review.notes: Route and its descent from the route page alone (rope length left out as a single-source figure); walk-in from the area page and further pages.

set.descent_text: The route finishes between two prominent aretes, after which you walk off to the west. An easy downclimb leads to the col between Mount Hooker and Tower Peak, and from there loose scree runs south back toward Pyramid Lake.
set.approach: Circle the west shore of Pyramid Lake, heading for the slabby south face of Mount Hooker. Work up slabs and grassy benches to a vertical band of broken but solid rock below the lower end of a left-leaning ramp, where the roped climbing begins.

review.notes: One route page supports both texts; the walk-in from the trailhead to Pyramid Lake is not given, so the approach begins at the lake.

set.approach: This is a long backcountry trip of roughly 14 to 16 miles each way from the Big Sandy trailhead, with Hailey Pass crossed in the later part of the walk. The trail ends among the boulders and meadows below the wall, and parties usually camp right at its foot. The other way in is from the Dickinson Park side. The route is on the northeast face, left of the nose and left of Hook, Line and Sinker. The start is near the highest point where the talus meets the wall: spot the quartz dike of pitch 5 and the green jade-coloured face of pitch 2, then trace them down to the paired diagonal cracks, like train tracks, that angle up to the right and make the first pitch.

review.notes: Start from the route page, face from the first-ascent account. Descent skipped: sources give only a rappel from the top of pitch 6, and none say how to leave the summit.
